projects.name: Cloud-Backed Portfolio
projects.purpose: Build a portfolio that is also a hands-on DevOps system, demonstrating cloud architecture, Infrastructure as Code, automated validation, secure cloud authentication, protected releases, serverless APIs, persistence, testing, and operational documentation.

architecture.frontend: HTML, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS hosted on GitHub Pages.
architecture.backend: Python 3.11 Azure Functions using the Python v2 programming model.
architecture.database: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL with PortfolioDB, Counter, and VisitorIPs containers.
architecture.infrastructure: Terraform with the AzureRM provider in Azure Korea Central.
architecture.terraform_state: Remote Terraform state stored in Azure Blob Storage.
architecture.ai: An OpenAI-compatible API integration through OpenCode Zen powers a portfolio-specific AI assistant.
architecture.authentication: GitHub Actions authenticates to Azure using GitHub OIDC federation with Microsoft Entra ID instead of a reusable Azure client secret.
architecture.branching: Two-branch model: dev for development/integration and main for protected production.

azure_resources: Standard LRS Storage Account for Azure Functions
Azure Cosmos DB account using the NoSQL API and free-tier configuration

cicd.development: Pushes to dev validate frontend files and JavaScript, Python dependencies and syntax, Ruff linting, pytest tests, and Terraform formatting/init/validate.
cicd.pull_request: A dev-to-main PR performs production-readiness validation including frontend artifact creation, backend dependency auditing, tests, Azure Function package creation, Azure OIDC authentication, remote-backend Terraform planning, and a final Production Ready gate.
cicd.production: Merges to main trigger path-specific workflows: frontend changes deploy to GitHub Pages, backend changes deploy to Azure Functions, and Terraform changes run production plan/apply.
cicd.concurrency: CI cancels obsolete development/PR runs while production Terraform deployment does not cancel in-progress applies.

security_and_reliability: Uses short-lived GitHub OIDC tokens for Azure authentication instead of storing an Azure service principal client secret.
Hashes visitor IP addresses with SHA-256 before storage.
Visitor/rate-limit records use a Cosmos DB TTL of 86400 seconds.
Backend dependencies are audited during PR validation.
Application and infrastructure changes are tested before production merge.
The AI client is lazily initialized so a missing AI API key cannot prevent Azure Functions from indexing unrelated routes.
The OpenCode API key is stored as a GitHub Actions secret and passed to Terraform as a sensitive variable to configure the Azure Function App environment.
features: Unique visitor counter backed by Cosmos DB.
Per-IP AI chat rate limit of 10 messages per hour.
Automated frontend, backend, and infrastructure deployment.
testing: pytest tests cover visitor-counter logic, AI chat behavior, route behavior, and lazy AI client initialization.
Tests use mocks/stubs and do not call real Azure Cosmos DB or the external AI provider.
operational_lessons: A deployment pipeline can report successful package deployment even when runtime routes are not healthy, so deployment success and runtime readiness should be treated as separate signals.
Optional external integrations should not be initialized at module import time because configuration failures can break function discovery.
The project roadmap includes post-deploy health checks and observability to detect runtime failures automatically.
cost_awareness: Uses Azure Functions Linux Consumption (Y1), Standard LRS storage, and Cosmos DB free tier to stay suitable for an Azure for Students subscription.
Jerome uses an Azure for Students subscription for this project.

projects.name: Enterprise GitOps Homelab
projects.experience_context: Personal home-lab project designed to apply production-style infrastructure and operational practices.
projects.purpose: Build a fully automated, self-healing, observable local Kubernetes environment using Infrastructure as Code and GitOps, with the Git repository acting as the source of truth.

architecture.virtualization: Proxmox virtual machines provisioned with Terraform.
architecture.gitops: Argo CD using the App-of-Apps pattern and sync waves.
architecture.networking: Calico CNI, MetalLB LoadBalancer IP address management, Traefik ingress, and Cert-Manager for TLS.
architecture.observability: Prometheus for metrics, Loki for logs, and Grafana for visualization.

gitops_workflow: Develop Terraform or Kubernetes YAML changes in Git.
GitHub Actions validates infrastructure/manifests using tools such as kubeconform and tflint.
Approved changes are merged to main.
Argo CD detects drift and reconciles the K3s cluster to the repository state.
engineering_practices: Infrastructure as Code for VM provisioning.
Sync waves for ordered application deployment.
CI quality gates for Helm/Kubernetes validation and security misconfiguration checks.
Separation between raw Kubernetes manifests and Helm value overrides.
Automated TLS, local DNS, distributed storage, and observability.
projects.disaster_recovery: The repository documents a bootstrap process intended to rebuild the cluster from bare metal in under 15 minutes by provisioning VMs, installing K3s/CNI, installing Argo CD, and applying the root App-of-Apps manifest.
problems_addressed: Invalid Kubernetes manifests and configuration errors

current_learning: Advanced cloud networking and hybrid-cloud topologies.
Optimizing Kubernetes deployments and GitOps workflows using Helm and Argo CD.
Integrating AI agents into CI/CD workflows for operational automation.
Cloud operations and observability practices for the portfolio, including health checks, monitoring, alerts, and post-deploy verification.

student_resources.azure: Uses an Azure for Students subscription and is intentionally cost-conscious when selecting Azure services and SKUs.

strengths: Hands-on learner who builds end-to-end systems rather than only studying tools in isolation.
Strong troubleshooting foundation from enterprise technical support.
Focus on automation, repeatability, and Infrastructure as Code.
Comfortable documenting architecture, CI/CD, security decisions, and operational procedures.
Actively applies production-oriented practices while clearly distinguishing personal projects from professional production experience.
